expectations.text: The transcript shows a Slack search bounded only by date before any chat finding is reported, and the Slack call log confirms its arguments: no topic keyword and no `from:` sender filter, with either a date term in the query or filters that includes Oct 1, 2026 (`on:2026-10-01`, `after:2026-09-30`, or a `before:`/`after:` pair spanning it) or `before`/`after` Unix timestamps spanning 2:00 PM to 2:45 PM (1790888400 to 1790891100). A keyword, sender, or channel-name search does not satisfy this, even if the conversations it found are read afterwards.
expectations.evidence: slack-calls.log first call: slack_search_public_and_private query 'on:2026-10-01', keywords [], filters '', no from:, all channel types. It precedes the turn-1 chat findings.

expectations.text: After the date-bounded search, the Slack call log shows `slack_read_channel` calls for Marcus's direct message (by `D0MARCUS`, `U0MARCUS`, or `marcus.hall`) and for the group direct message (`G0RELLEADS` or its name); the log records calls in order, so each read must appear below that search. Each read's `oldest` is empty or at most 1790888400 and its `latest` is empty or at least 1790891100, so it covers 2:00 PM to 2:45 PM. A search scoped to the conversation does not count as a read, and a read made before the date-bounded search does not satisfy this.
expectations.evidence: Below that search in slack-calls.log: slack_read_channel D0MARCUS and G0RELLEADS, each oldest 1790888400, latest 1790891100. Also read C0REL42 over the same window, which returned no messages.
